verdict: Salesforce closed its fiscal year with revenue up 12% to $11.2B — including $399M from the newly acquired Informatica — and an $811M paper gain on its investments padded net income to $1.9B.

segments.name: Subscription and support
segments.note: The core software subscriptions — Sales, Service, Slack, Tableau, Agentforce and Data 360 — including $388M contributed by Informatica.

segments.name: Professional services and other
segments.note: Consulting and training that help customers roll the software out.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the platform — including Agentforce, Salesforce's AI agents, and Data 360 — up 14% YoY.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: The largest running cost — Salesforce's big sales force and marketing machine, up 16% YoY.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day — up 18% YoY.

opex.name: Restructuring
opex.note: One-off costs of reorganizing teams — roughly flat vs $298M a year ago.

takeaways.title: Backlog at a record
takeaways.text: Remaining performance obligation — work customers have signed for but not yet paid — hit $72.4B, up 14%, with $35.1B of it due within a year. Future revenue is unusually visible.

takeaways.title: A paper gain padded profit
takeaways.text: Gains on strategic investments added $811M before tax ($0.66 a share after tax). Core operating income was $1.87B, barely up from $1.82B a year ago — the gain is real on paper, but it isn't the software business selling more.

takeaways.title: Agentforce is scaling
takeaways.text: Agentforce ARR reached $800M, up 169% YoY, with 29,000 deals closed — Salesforce's AI agents are becoming a real revenue line, though still small next to $10.7B of subscription revenue.

oneTimers: An $811M gain on strategic investments — paper (mark-to-market) gains on stakes Salesforce holds in other companies; it added $0.66 to diluted EPS.
Revenue includes $399M from Informatica, acquired in late 2025 — roughly 3–4 points of the 12% growth is the acquisition, not organic growth.
otherDetail: An $811M paper gain on strategic investments (stakes Salesforce holds in other companies), partly offset by $52M of other expense, net — mostly interest on Salesforce's debt, net of interest earned.
